original_query: select * from emp where empno > ANY (  select deptno from dept where emp.job = dept.name);
rewritten_query:
SELECT e.*
FROM emp e
JOIN (
    SELECT name, MIN(deptno) AS min_deptno
    FROM dept
    GROUP BY name
) d ON d.name = e.job
WHERE e.empno > d.min_deptno;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Rewrite `empno > ANY (SELECT deptno FROM dept WHERE emp.job = dept.name)` as a join against a pre-aggregated derived table. Since `x > ANY(S)` is equivalent to `x > MIN(S)` over non-null values, grouping dept by name with MIN(deptno) eliminates duplicate probes and the extra join filter. Rewrite score: 90/100.
Avoid `SELECT *` in production if only a subset of columns is needed; this reduces I/O over the 45M-row emp table and can enable covering-index plans. Rewrite score: 80/100.

Support the rewrite with an index on dept(name, deptno) to speed the GROUP BY/min computation, and consider emp(job, empno) if the join is highly selective. With ~14M expected output rows, a seq scan + hash join on emp is likely still optimal. Rewrite score: 85/100.

The `> ANY` correlated subquery was converted into an explicit join predicate `e.empno > d.min_deptno`, which is semantically equivalent (including NULL and empty-set behavior) and simplifies the plan. Rewrite score: 90/100.
